changes.year1_quote: This section highlights significant factors, events, and uncertainties that make an investment in our securities risky.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: The following discussion sets forth what management currently believes could be the material risks and uncertainties that could impact our businesses, results of operations and financial condition.
changes.reasoning: The Year-2 disclosure continues to address the same overarching economic risk: material risks and uncertainties that may adversely affect the company and its securities. The wording and framing changed, but the substantive risk scope and consequences remain materially the same.
changes.title: Risk Factors Overview and Scope

changes.year1_quote: Changes and instability in the macroeconomic environment, consumer confidence and customer behavior may adversely affect our business.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: Changes and instability in the macroeconomic environment, consumer confidence and customer behavior may adversely affect our business.
changes.reasoning: The Year-2022 summary retains the same underlying macroeconomic, consumer-confidence, and customer-behavior risks with materially identical economic substance. Although several individual bullets have minor wording changes or additions, the principal risk disclosure as a whole remains present rather than being softened or removed.
changes.title: Summary of Principal Risk Factors

changes.year1_quote: Although the global economy has begun to recover from the COVID-19 pandemic and many health and safety restrictions have been lifted and vaccine distribution has increased, certain adverse consequences of the pandemic, especially as a result of the emergence of the Omicron variant in late 2021, continue to impact the macroeconomic environment and may persist for some time.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: Although the global economy has begun to recover from the COVID-19 pandemic, certain adverse consequences of the pandemic, including labor shortages, disruptions of global supply chains and inflationary pressures, continue to impact the macroeconomic environment and could adversely affect our business.
changes.reasoning: The core economic risks—pandemic-related macroeconomic effects, labor shortages, supply-chain disruptions, inflation, weaker demand, credit losses, asset impairments, and liquidity/capital pressure—remain disclosed in Year-2. The added hybrid-work discussion is an additional operational risk, not a material change to the Year-1 pandemic economic-risk disclosure.
changes.title: COVID-19 Pandemic Business Impacts

changes.year1_quote: These measures could impair our ability to perform critical functions and may adversely impact our results of operations. In addition, these measures and other changes in consumer behavior as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic may require changes to retail distribution strategies and adversely impact our investments in our bank premises and equipment and other retail distribution assets, leading to increased costs and exposure to additional risks.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: In the third quarter of 2022, we moved our associates to a hybrid work model. As a result we may experience increased costs and/or disruption as we experiment with hybrid work models, in addition to potential effects on our ability to operate effectively and maintain our corporate culture. We will continue to monitor local conditions to ensure the safety of our associates and customers while providing critical banking services. ... These measures could impair our ability to perform critical functions and may adversely impact our results of operations.
changes.reasoning: The operational disruption risk from COVID-19 measures, including effects on critical functions and increased costs, remains explicitly disclosed in Year-2 and is supplemented by hybrid-work disruption risks. However, the specific Year-1 risk concerning changes to retail distribution strategies and impairment of bank-premises and other retail-distribution assets is not separately stated; it is best treated as absorbed within the broader COVID-19 operational-effects disclosure.
changes.title: COVID-19 Operational and Program Risks

changes.year1_quote: Our participation in and execution of any such programs may cause operational, compliance, reputational and credit risks, which could result in litigation, governmental action or other forms of loss.
changes.reasoning: No Year-2 candidate meaningfully addresses the economic risk associated with participating in COVID-19 governmental relief programs, including related operational, compliance, reputational, credit, litigation, or governmental-action risks. The disclosure is therefore classified as removed.
changes.title: COVID-19 Government Programs and Uncertainty

changes.year1_quote: The extent to which the consequences of the COVID-19 pandemic affect our businesses, results of operations and financial condition, as well as our regulatory capital and liquidity ratios and our ability to take capital actions, will depend on future developments that remain uncertain...
changes.year2_quote_or_null: Long-term consequences of the COVID-19 pandemic on our business, results of operations and financial condition, as well as our capital and liquidity ratios and our ability to take capital actions, will depend on future developments that remain uncertain, including, for example, future actions taken by governmental authorities, central banks and other third parties in response to the pandemic and the effects on our customers, counterparties, associates and third-party service providers.
changes.reasoning: The core economic risk is retained: uncertain future COVID-19 developments may affect the business, results, financial condition, capital and liquidity ratios, and ability to take capital actions. Year-2022 also adds specific ongoing pandemic effects and potential adverse consequences, but does not materially eliminate or weaken the Year-2021 risk.
changes.title: COVID-19 Future Developments and Effects

changes.year1_quote: Changes and instability in the macroeconomic environment, consumer confidence and customer behavior may adversely affect our business.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: Changes and instability in the macroeconomic environment, consumer confidence and customer behavior may adversely affect our business.
changes.reasoning: The core economic risk—macroeconomic deterioration and changes in consumer confidence and customer behavior adversely affecting financial condition and results—is expressly retained. Year-2 adds related risks and expands some examples, but does not weaken or remove the Year-1 disclosure.
changes.title: Macroeconomic Conditions and Customer Behavior

changes.year1_quote: Although this deal provides greater near-term stability, there is still some degree of uncertainty as to the relationship between the U.K and the European Union, which may increase volatility in the regional and global financial markets.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: Although this deal has provided greater near-term stability, there is still some degree of uncertainty as to the relationship between the U.K and the EU, which may increase volatility in the regional and global financial markets.
changes.reasoning: The Year-2022 disclosure preserves the same underlying economic risk: continuing uncertainty in the U.K.–EU relationship after Brexit may increase regional and global financial-market volatility. It is also expressly retained within the broader macroeconomic-risk discussion, but the risk itself remains materially unchanged.
changes.title: U.K. and European Union Economic Uncertainty

changes.year1_quote: A flat yield curve combined with low interest rates generally leads to lower revenue and reduced margins because it can decrease the spread between asset yields and funding costs.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: Additionally, a shrinking yield premium between short-term and long-term market interest rates and in the relationship between our funding basis rate and our lending basis rate and inflation could affect our profitability.
changes.reasoning: The Year-2022 disclosure retains the underlying economic risks from capital-market disruption, interest-rate changes, funding costs, and reduced spreads/net interest income, while bundling the Year-2021 financial-market-instability discussion into a broader “Interest Rates and Capital Markets” unit. The specific low-rate/flat-curve formulation is not retained verbatim, but the spread and profitability risk remains explicitly addressed.
changes.title: Financial Market Instability and Volatility

changes.year1_quote: We may experience increased delinquencies, credit losses, inaccurate estimates and inadequate reserves.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: We may experience increases or fluctuations in delinquencies and credit losses, inaccurate estimates and inadequate reserves.
changes.reasoning: The underlying economic risk is unchanged: customer nonrepayment may lead to delinquencies and credit losses, with related estimation and reserve risks. The addition of “or fluctuations” does not materially alter the substance or severity of the disclosure.
changes.title: Credit Risk and Repayment Exposure

changes.year1_quote: Historically, customers are more likely to miss payments during an economic downturn or prolonged periods of slow economic growth. In addition, we face the risk that consumer and commercial customer behavior may change ... causing a long-term rise in delinquencies and charge-offs.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: Historically, customers are more likely to miss payments during an economic downturn, recession, periods of high unemployment, or prolonged periods of slow economic growth. In addition, we face the risk that consumer and commercial customer behavior may change ... causing a long-term rise or fluctuations in delinquencies and charge-offs.
changes.reasoning: The Year-2 disclosure retains the same underlying economic risk: adverse economic conditions and changes in customer repayment behavior may increase missed payments, delinquencies, and charge-offs. It adds examples of recession and high unemployment and notes possible fluctuations rather than only a long-term rise, but these are substantive elaborations rather than a material weakening or removal of the risk.
changes.title: Credit Risk — Missed Payments

changes.year1_quote: We may underestimate our expected losses and fail to hold an allowance for credit losses sufficient to account for these losses.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: We may underestimate our expected losses and fail to hold an allowance for credit losses sufficient to account for these losses.
changes.reasoning: The Year-2 disclosure preserves the same economic risk: inaccurate judgments or assumptions may cause expected credit losses to be underestimated and the allowance for credit losses to be inadequate. The added cross-reference to model and data risks does not change or weaken the underlying disclosure.
changes.title: Credit Risk — Expected Loss Estimates

changes.year1_quote: Our ability to accurately assess the creditworthiness of our customers may diminish, which could result in an increase in our credit losses and a deterioration of our returns.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: Our ability to assess the creditworthiness of our customers may be impaired if the models and approaches we use to select, manage and underwrite our consumer and commercial customers become less predictive of future charge-offs due, for example, to rapid changes in the economy, or degradation in the predictive nature of credit bureau and other data used in underwriting.
changes.reasoning: The underlying economic risk—impaired ability to assess customer creditworthiness, leading to higher credit losses and poorer returns—is expressly preserved in Candidate 2, with additional detail on underwriting models, data, and future charge-offs. Candidate 1 is substantively identical to the Year-1 disclosure, so the risk was retained rather than merely absorbed or removed.
changes.title: Credit Risk — Underwriting Accuracy

changes.year1_quote: Because we originate a relatively greater proportion of consumer loans in our loan portfolio compared to other large bank peers and originate both prime and subprime credit card accounts and auto loans, we may experience higher delinquencies and a greater number of accounts charging off compared to other large bank peers, which could result in increased credit losses, operating costs and regulatory scrutiny.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: Because we originate a relatively greater proportion of consumer loans in our loan portfolio compared to other large bank peers and originate both prime and subprime credit card accounts and auto loans, we may experience higher delinquencies and a greater number of accounts charging off, as well as greater fluctuations in those metrics, compared to other large bank peers, which could result in increased credit losses, operating costs and regulatory scrutiny.
changes.reasoning: The underlying economic risk is retained: a consumer-heavy mix, including subprime products, may produce higher delinquencies, charge-offs, credit losses, costs, and scrutiny. Year-2 adds potential fluctuations in delinquency and charge-off metrics but does not weaken or materially alter the risk.
changes.title: Credit Risk — Business Mix

changes.year1_quote: Adoption of the CECL standard has resulted and may continue to result in an increase to our reserves for credit losses on financial instruments with a resulting adverse impact on our financial condition.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: The impact of measuring our allowance for credit losses on our results will depend on the characteristics of our financial instruments, economic conditions, and our economic and loss forecasts.
changes.reasoning: The Year-2 disclosure retains the CECL-related reserve and earnings risk, including the possibility of faster and higher reserve increases in downturns, but removes the statement that CECL adoption has resulted and may continue to result in increased reserves with an adverse impact on financial condition. This materially weakens the asserted impact while preserving the underlying risk.
changes.title: Credit Risk — CECL and Reserve Recognition

changes.year1_quote: The collateral we have on secured loans could be insufficient to compensate us for credit losses.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: The collateral we have on secured loans could be insufficient to compensate us for credit losses.
changes.reasoning: The Year-2 disclosure reproduces the same economic risk, including the risk that collateral values may be insufficient to cover secured-loan credit losses and the related commercial real estate and auto collateral exposures. No material qualifier or scope change is evident.
changes.title: Credit Risk — Collateral and Asset Values

changes.year1_quote: Although our consumer lending is geographically diversified, approximately 45% of our commercial real estate loan portfolio is concentrated in the Northeast region.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: Although our consumer lending is geographically diversified, approximately 40% of our commercial real estate loan portfolio is concentrated in the Northeast region.
changes.reasoning: The underlying geographic concentration risk and its potential impact on commercial real estate performance remain disclosed, but the stated concentration declined from approximately 45% to 40%, reducing the magnitude of the disclosed exposure. The industry-specific concentration risk and adverse-impact language are otherwise materially retained.
changes.title: Geographic and Industry Concentration

changes.year1_quote: We may not be able to maintain adequate capital or liquidity levels, which could have a negative impact on our financial results and our ability to return capital to our stockholders.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: We may not be able to maintain adequate capital or liquidity levels or may become subject to revised capital or liquidity requirements, which could have a negative impact on our financial results and our ability to return capital to our stockholders.
changes.reasoning: The Year-2022 disclosure retains the same underlying economic risk of inadequate capital or liquidity and adds exposure to revised requirements. The related consequences and regulatory remedies are also materially preserved, so the change is not a weakening or removal of the Year-2021 risk.
changes.title: Capital and Liquidity Adequacy

changes.year1_quote: There can be significant differences between our modeling and the Federal Reserve’s projections for a given supervisory stress scenario and between the capital needs suggested by our internal stress scenarios relative to the supervisory scenarios.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: There can be significant differences between our modeling and the Federal Reserve’s projections for a given supervisory stress scenario and between the capital needs suggested by our internal stress scenarios and the supervisory scenarios.
changes.reasoning: Candidate 1 retains the same economic risk: differences between internal and Federal Reserve stress-test projections may indicate lower capital capacity and restrict dividends or share repurchases. The wording adds context about the stress capital buffer requirement but does not materially change the risk.
changes.title: Capital Stress Testing and Distributions

changes.year1_quote: Regulatory liquidity stress testing and regulatory liquidity requirements may, therefore, require us to take actions to increase our liquid assets or alter our activities or funding sources, which could negatively affect our financial results or our ability to return capital to our stockholders.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: Regulatory liquidity stress testing and regulatory liquidity requirements may, therefore, require us to take actions to increase our liquid assets or alter our activities or funding sources, which could negatively affect our financial results or our ability to return capital to our stockholders.
changes.reasoning: Candidate 1 addresses the same economic risk—regulatory and internal liquidity stress tests may produce differing liquidity needs, and regulatory requirements may force increased liquid assets or changes to activities or funding that could harm results or capital returns. The disclosure is materially unchanged; Candidate 2 concerns capital stress testing and does not replace the liquidity risk.
changes.title: Liquidity Stress Testing and Requirements

changes.year1_quote: Although these temporary restrictions on our capital actions ended on June 30, 2021, it is possible that the Federal Reserve could impose similar restrictions in the future.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: In addition, changes to applicable capital and liquidity requirements could result in increased expenses or unexpected or new limitations on our ability to pay dividends and engage in share repurchases.
changes.reasoning: The Year-2 disclosure retains the economic risk of limitations on dividends and share repurchases arising from capital and liquidity requirements, but no longer specifically states that the Federal Reserve could reimpose restrictions on capital actions. The pandemic-related and direct regulatory-restriction risk is therefore narrowed and softened, while the remaining requirements risk is still disclosed.
changes.title: Restrictions on Capital Actions

changes.year1_quote: Limitations on our ability to receive dividends from our subsidiaries could affect our liquidity and ability to pay dividends and repurchase common stock.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: Limitations on our ability to receive dividends from our subsidiaries could affect our liquidity and ability to pay dividends and repurchase common stock.
changes.reasoning: The Year-2 disclosure retains the same underlying economic risk: legal, regulatory, and supervisory limits on subsidiary distributions could constrain the parent’s liquidity, shareholder payments, repurchases, and other obligations. Although the wording and some details changed (including an explicit reference to capital distributions and regulatory limitations), the risk was not materially weakened or removed.
changes.title: Subsidiary Dividend Limitations

changes.year1_quote: Digital technology, data and software development are deeply embedded into our business model and how we work.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: Digital technology, cloud-based services, data and software development are deeply embedded into our business model and how we work.
changes.reasoning: The underlying operational, technological, and organizational infrastructure risk is unchanged. Year 2 adds cloud-based services to the list of embedded technologies, which expands specificity but does not materially alter the economic risk disclosed.
changes.title: Operational Technology and Infrastructure

changes.year1_quote: We also are subject to disruptions to our systems arising from events that are wholly or partially beyond our control, which may include computer viruses, electrical or telecommunications outages, design flaws in foundational components or platforms, availability and quality of vulnerability patches from key vendors, cyber-attacks and other security incidents (including Distributed Denial of Service (“DDOS”) and other attacks on our infrastructure as discussed below), natural disasters, other damage to property or physical assets, or events arising from local or larger scale politics, including terrorist acts.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: We also are subject to disruptions to our systems arising from events that are wholly or partially beyond our control, which may include computer viruses, electrical or telecommunications outages, bugs, design flaws in foundational components or platforms, availability and quality of vulnerability patches from key vendors, cyber-attacks and other security incidents, natural disasters, other damage to property or physical assets, or events arising from local or larger scale politics, including terrorist acts.
changes.reasoning: The core economic risk—operational failures and externally caused technology or system disruptions impairing operations, customer service, information protection, reputation, and regulatory standing—remains materially present in Year-2. The added fraud and near-real-time payments language expands the disclosure, while deletion of the DDOS parenthetical and minor wording changes do not alter the underlying risk.
changes.title: Operational Disruptions and Resiliency

changes.year1_quote: If we fail to administer these new environments in a well-managed, secure and effective manner, or if such platforms become unavailable or do not meet their service level agreements for any reason, we may experience unplanned service disruption or unforeseen costs which could result in material harm to our business and results of operations.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: If we fail to architect, administer or oversee these environments in a well-managed, secure and effective manner, or if such platforms become unavailable, are disrupted, fail to scale, do not operate as designed, or do not meet their service level agreements for any reason, we may experience unplanned service disruption or unforeseen costs which could result in material harm to our business and operations.
changes.reasoning: The Year-2 disclosure retains the same underlying economic risk: reliance on outsourced AWS and other cloud providers could cause outages, security incidents, service disruptions, increased costs, and material harm. It adds operational failure modes such as failure to scale and expands the provider incident examples, but does not weaken or remove the risk.
changes.title: Third-Party Cloud and Technology Dependencies

changes.year1_quote: Any disruptions, failures or inaccuracies of our operational processes, technology systems and models, including those associated with improvements or modifications to such technology systems and models, could cause us to be unable to market and manage our products and services, manage our risk, meet our regulatory obligations or report our financial results in a timely and accurate manner, all of which could have a negative impact on our results of operations.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: Any disruptions, failures or inaccuracies of our operational processes, technology systems and models, including those associated with improvements or modifications to such technology systems and models, could cause us to be unable to market and manage our products and services, manage our risk, meet our regulatory obligations or report our financial results in a timely and accurate manner, all of which could have a negative impact on our results of operations.
changes.reasoning: The Year-2 disclosure reproduces the Year-1 economic risks, including operational and technology failures, expense increases, and ineffective change-management governance, with no material weakening, negation, or removal. The differences are limited to the heading and do not change the underlying risk.
changes.title: Operational Processes, Expenses and Change

changes.year1_quote: A cyber-attack or other security incident, including one that results in the theft, loss or misuse of information (including personal information), or the disabling of systems and access to information critical to business operations, may result in increased costs, reductions in revenue, reputational damage, legal exposure and business disruptions.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: A cyber-attack or other security incident, including one that results in the theft, loss, manipulation or misuse of information (including personal information), or the disabling of systems and access to information critical to business operations, may result in increased costs, reductions in revenue, reputational damage, legal exposure and business disruptions.
changes.reasoning: The core economic risk—cybersecurity incidents causing information compromise, system disabling, and resulting financial, legal, reputational, and operational harm—is expressly retained in Candidate 1. The added “manipulation” example and other expanded detail do not change the underlying risk, and Candidate 2 independently repeats the same risk in its summary.
changes.title: Cybersecurity and Information Security Risk

changes.year1_quote: Technologies, systems, networks, and other devices of Capital One, as well as those of our employees, service providers, partners and other third parties with whom we interact, have been and may continue to be the subject of cyber-attacks and other security incidents, including DDOS attacks, computer viruses, hacking, malware, ransomware, credential stuffing, or phishing or other forms of social engineering.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: Technologies, systems, networks, and other devices of Capital One, as well as those of our employees, service providers, partners and other third parties with whom we interact, have been and may continue to be the subject of cyber-attacks and other security incidents, including computer viruses, hacking, malware, ransomware, supply chain attacks, vulnerabilities, credential stuffing, or phishing or other forms of social engineering.
changes.reasoning: The underlying economic risk—cyber-attacks and security incidents affecting Capital One and connected third parties, with potential unauthorized access, information compromise, service disruption, fraud, and illicit use—remains materially intact. Year-2022 adds some attack types and separately states business, legal, revenue, cost, and reputational impacts, but does not weaken or remove the Year-2021 risk.
changes.title: Cyber-Attack Methods and Impacts

changes.year1_quote: Cyber and information security risks for large financial institutions like us continue to increase due to the proliferation of new technologies, the industry-wide shift to reliance upon the internet to conduct financial transactions, and the increased sophistication and activities of malicious actors, organized crime, perpetrators of fraud, hackers, terrorists, activists, formal and informal instrumentalities of foreign governments and other external parties.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: Cyber and information security risks for large financial institutions like us continue to increase due to the proliferation of new technologies, the industry-wide shift to reliance upon the internet to conduct financial transactions, and the increased sophistication and activities of malicious actors, organized crime, perpetrators of fraud, hackers, terrorists, activists, extremist parties, formal and informal instrumentalities of foreign governments, state-sponsored actors and other external parties.
changes.reasoning: The core economic risks—cyberattack, unauthorized access, data loss, fraud, third-party breach exposure, and increasing threats from technology, remote operations, and malicious actors—remain disclosed in Year-2. The language is modestly updated and adds remote/hybrid-work and mobile/cloud expansion risks, but it does not materially reduce or eliminate the Year-1 exposure.
changes.title: 2019 Cybersecurity Incident and Threats

changes.year1_quote: The methods and techniques employed by malicious actors change frequently, are increasingly sophisticated and often are not fully recognized or understood until after they have occurred, and some techniques could occur and persist for an extended period of time before being detected.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: The methods and techniques employed by malicious actors change frequently, are increasingly sophisticated and often are not fully recognized or understood until after they have occurred, and some techniques could occur and persist for an extended period of time before being detected and remediated.
changes.reasoning: Candidate 1 retains the same underlying economic risk: increasingly sophisticated attacks may evade timely detection, mitigation, or remediation, including limitations in controls, third parties, and cybersecurity talent. The added or expanded language is not a material downgrade or removal of the risk; the disclosure is substantively reworded and slightly expanded.
changes.title: Cybersecurity Detection and Mitigation Challenges

changes.year1_quote: A disruption or breach, including as a result of a cyber-attack such as the Cybersecurity Incident, or media reports of perceived security vulnerabilities at Capital One or at our service providers, could result in significant legal and financial exposure, regulatory intervention, litigation, remediation costs, card reissuance, supervisory liability, damage to our reputation or loss of confidence in the security of our systems, products and services that could adversely affect our business.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: A disruption or breach, including as a result of a cyber-attack such as the Cybersecurity Incident, or media reports of perceived security vulnerabilities at Capital One or at our service providers, could result in significant legal and financial exposure, regulatory intervention, litigation, remediation costs, card reissuance, supervisory liability, damage to our reputation or loss of confidence in the security of our systems, products and services that could adversely affect our business.
changes.reasoning: The Year-2 candidate reproduces the Year-1 disclosure verbatim, including the same cyber incident scenarios, third-party exposure, operational impacts, and potential legal, financial, regulatory, and reputational consequences. The underlying economic risk is unchanged.
changes.title: Cyber Incidents — Business and Financial Impact

changes.year1_quote: Further, our ability to monitor our service providers’ cybersecurity practices is limited. Although we generally have agreements relating to cybersecurity and data privacy in place with our service providers, we cannot guarantee that such agreements will prevent a cyber incident impacting our systems or information or enable us to obtain adequate or any reimbursement from our service providers in the event we should suffer any such incidents.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: Further, our ability to monitor our service providers’ cybersecurity practices is limited. Although the agreements that we have in place with our service providers generally include requirements relating to cybersecurity and data privacy, we cannot guarantee that such agreements will prevent a cyber incident impacting our systems or information or enable us to obtain adequate or any reimbursement from our service providers in the event we should suffer any such incidents.
changes.reasoning: The Year-2 disclosure preserves the same economic risks: limited oversight, inability to ensure prevention or reimbursement, and responsibility for incidents involving shared information. The changes are grammatical and do not alter the risk, qualifiers, or allocation of liability.
changes.title: Service Providers — Cybersecurity Oversight

changes.year1_quote: In addition, the increasing prevalence and the evolution of cyber-attacks and other efforts to breach or disrupt our systems or networks or those of our customers, service providers, partners or other third parties with which we interact has led, and will likely continue to lead, to increased costs to us with respect to preventing, mitigating and remediating these risks, as well as any related attempted fraud.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: In addition, the increasing prevalence and the evolution of cyber-attacks and other efforts to breach or disrupt our systems or networks or those of our customers, service providers, partners or other third parties with which we interact has led, and will likely continue to lead, to increased costs to us with respect to preventing, detecting, mitigating and remediating these risks, as well as any related attempted fraud.
changes.reasoning: The Year-2 disclosure retains the same underlying economic risks: cyberattacks, response and remediation costs, customer-confidence effects, required security investment, and insurance limitations. The addition of “detecting” and replacement of “financial system” with “global financial system” do not materially change the risk.
changes.title: Cybersecurity — Costs, Confidence and Insurance

changes.year1_quote: Our required compliance with applicable laws and regulations related to privacy, data protection and data security may increase our costs, reduce our revenue, increase our legal exposure and limit our ability to pursue business opportunities.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: Our required compliance with applicable laws and regulations related to privacy, data protection and data security may increase our costs, reduce our revenue, increase our legal exposure and limit our ability to pursue business opportunities.
changes.reasoning: The Year-2 Candidate 1 reproduces the Year-1 economic risk verbatim and expands it with examples of evolving privacy and data-security laws. Candidate 2 also repeats the risk in its summary, so the disclosure was retained rather than materially changed or absorbed.
changes.title: Privacy and Data Security — Compliance Costs

changes.year1_quote: We are subject to a variety of continuously evolving and developing laws and regulations in the United States at the federal, state and local level regarding privacy, data protection and data security, including those related to the collection, storage, handling, use, disclosure, transfer, security and other processing of personal information.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: We are subject to a variety of continuously evolving and developing laws and regulations in the United States at the federal, state and local level regarding privacy, data protection and data security, including those related to the collection, storage, handling, use, disclosure, transfer, security and other processing of personal information.
changes.reasoning: Candidate 1 retains the same underlying economic risk: exposure to continuously evolving U.S. privacy, data-protection, and data-security requirements, including federal incident-notification and state-law obligations. It adds potential cost, revenue, legal-exposure, and business-opportunity consequences but does not weaken or remove the Year-1 risk.
changes.title: U.S. Privacy Laws — Evolving Requirements

changes.year1_quote: These laws and regulations, and similar laws and regulations in other jurisdictions, impose strict requirements regarding the collection, storage, handling, use, disclosure, transfer, security and other processing of personal information, which may have adverse consequences, including significant compliance costs and severe monetary penalties for non-compliance.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: These laws and regulations, and similar laws and regulations in other jurisdictions, impose strict requirements regarding the collection, storage, handling, use, disclosure, transfer, security and other processing of personal information, which may have adverse consequences, including significant compliance costs and severe monetary penalties for non-compliance.
changes.reasoning: Candidate 1 retains the same underlying economic risk: evolving international privacy laws impose strict data-processing requirements, create compliance uncertainty, and may result in significant costs and severe penalties. The minor wording changes do not alter the substance, and Candidate 2 addresses additional U.S. privacy risks rather than replacing this disclosure.
changes.title: International Privacy Laws — Compliance Uncertainty

changes.year1_quote: The publication of our privacy policies and other statements that provide promises and assurances about privacy, data protection and data security can subject us to potential government or legal action if they are found to be deceptive, unfair or misrepresentative of our actual practices.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: The publication of our privacy policies and other statements that provide promises and assurances about privacy, data protection and data security can subject us to potential government or legal action if they are found to be deceptive, unfair or misrepresentative of our actual practices.
changes.reasoning: The Year-2 candidate is substantively identical to the Year-1 disclosure: it retains the risk of government or legal action arising from privacy statements that are deceptive, unfair, or misrepresentative, as well as the risk of failing to meet those statements.
changes.title: Privacy Disclosures — Public Statements and Liability

changes.year1_quote: Our efforts to comply with PIPEDA, GLBA, GDPR, U.K. GDPR, CCPA, CPRA and other privacy, data protection and data security laws and regulations, as well as our posted privacy policies, and related contractual obligations to third parties, entail substantial expenses, may divert resources from other initiatives and projects, and could limit the services we are able to offer.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: Our efforts to comply with GLBA, CPRA, PIPEDA, EU GDPR, U.K. GDPR and other privacy, data protection and data security laws and regulations, as well as our posted privacy policies, and related contractual obligations to third parties, entail substantial expenses, may divert resources from other initiatives and projects, and could limit the services we are able to offer.
changes.reasoning: The Year-2 disclosure retains the same economic risks: substantial compliance costs, resource diversion, service limitations, increasing enforcement, and potential business restrictions, penalties, reputational harm, and legal liability. The differences are limited to the ordering of laws and the omission of CCPA as a separately named law, while CPRA remains listed; these do not materially change the underlying risk.
changes.title: Privacy Compliance — Enforcement and Business Restrictions

changes.year1_quote: We face risks resulting from the extensive use of models and data.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: We face risks resulting from the extensive use of models and data.
changes.reasoning: The Year-2022 disclosure retains the same underlying economic risks: reliance on models and data for risk assessment, reporting, forecasting, regulatory capital, and financial estimates, including model limitations, data quality issues, manual processes, and potential losses. The wording adds modeling and data limitations but does not materially downgrade or eliminate the risk.
changes.title: Models and Data — Risk Management Reliance

changes.title: Interest Rates and Customer Behavior

changes.year1_quote: We face the risk that changes in interest rates could materially reduce our net interest income and our earnings, especially if actual conditions turn out to be materially different than those we assumed.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: We face the risk that changes in interest rates could materially reduce our net interest income and our earnings, especially if actual conditions turn out to be materially different than those we assumed.
changes.reasoning: The Year-2 disclosure reproduces the same underlying economic risk: interest-rate changes, particularly when different from assumptions, may materially reduce net interest income and earnings. It also retains the Year-1 scenario-based assessment of effects on earnings, economic value, and capital, so this is not merely absorbed into the broader interest-rate discussion.
changes.title: Interest Rate Risk Assessment

changes.year1_quote: A transition away from the widespread use of LIBOR to alternative rates and other potential interest rate benchmark reforms has begun and is continuing. These reforms have caused and may in the future cause such rates to perform differently than in the past, or to disappear entirely, or have other consequences which cannot be predicted.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: A transition away from the use of LIBOR to alternative rates and other potential interest rate benchmark reforms is not yet complete. These reforms have caused and may in the future cause such rates to perform differently than in the past, or to disappear entirely, or have other consequences which cannot be predicted.
changes.reasoning: The core economic risk—adverse consequences from the ongoing transition away from LIBOR and benchmark reform, including rates changing or disappearing—remains explicitly disclosed in Year-2. Year-2 adds more detailed residual exposure and implementation risks, but does not materially reduce or eliminate the Year-1 risk.
changes.title: LIBOR Transition and Benchmark Reform

changes.year1_quote: We have loans, derivative contracts, unsecured debt, securitizations, vendor agreements and other instruments with attributes that are either directly or indirectly dependent on LIBOR.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: While we have substantially decreased our exposure to LIBOR, we have certain loans, derivative contracts, securitizations, and other contracts with attributes that are either directly or indirectly dependent on LIBOR.
changes.reasoning: The underlying LIBOR-transition risk is retained and expanded, including continuing market, legal, operational, systems, and model risks. However, Year-2 expressly states that exposure has been substantially decreased and omits some Year-1 instrument categories (such as unsecured debt and vendor agreements), signaling a reduced level of exposure rather than a purely cosmetic rewrite.
changes.title: LIBOR-Linked Instruments and Transition Risks

changes.year1_quote: Our assessment of the ultimate impact of, and our planning for, the transition from LIBOR remains ongoing. Failure to adequately manage the transition could have a material adverse effect on our reputation, business, financial condition and results of operations.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: While we have substantially decreased our exposure to LIBOR, we have certain loans, derivative contracts, securitizations, and other contracts with attributes that are either directly or indirectly dependent on LIBOR.
changes.reasoning: The Year-2 disclosure retains the core economic risks—outstanding LIBOR-linked contracts, transition uncertainty, differing payments, systems and operational disruption, and potential material adverse effects—but softens the exposure framing by stating that Capital One has substantially decreased its LIBOR exposure and largely remediated the majority of exposures. The remaining transition risks are still expressly disclosed, so this is not removal.
changes.title: Outstanding LIBOR Contracts and Systems

changes.year1_quote: Our business could be negatively affected if we are unable to attract, retain and motivate skilled employees.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: Our business could be negatively affected if we are unable to attract, retain and motivate key senior leaders and skilled employees.
changes.reasoning: The core economic risk—failure to attract, retain, and motivate skilled employees and senior leaders harming the business—is expressly preserved. Year-2 adds specificity about key senior leaders and replaces the Year-1 external-environment detail with succession-planning discussion, but does not weaken or remove the underlying risk.
changes.title: Attracting and Retaining Skilled Employees

changes.year1_quote: Natural disasters and other catastrophic events could harm our employees, business and infrastructure, including our information technology systems and third-party platforms.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: Geopolitical events, natural disasters and other catastrophic events could harm our employees, business and infrastructure, including our information technology systems and third-party platforms.
changes.reasoning: The core catastrophic-event and business-continuity risk is retained, but Year-2 removes the explicit reference to climate change as a cause of extreme weather and no longer describes the COVID-19-related remote-work response example. These omissions narrow and soften the disclosed scope of the risk, despite adding geopolitical events and third-party-platform location risk.
changes.title: Unpredictable Catastrophic Events

changes.year1_quote: Climate change manifesting as physical or transition risks could adversely affect our operations, businesses and customers.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: Climate change manifesting as physical or transition risks could adversely affect our businesses, operations and customers.
changes.reasoning: The core economic risk is retained: Year-2022 continues to disclose adverse physical and transition climate effects on the company, customers and relied-upon third parties, with the physical, transition, financial/customer, reputational, and risk-management aspects addressed across Candidates 1–4. The disclosures are reorganized and in some respects expanded, but do not negate or materially downgrade the Year-2021 risk.
changes.title: Physical and Transition Climate Risks

changes.year1_quote: We face risks from the use of or changes to assumptions or estimates in our financial statements.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: We face risks from the use of or changes to assumptions or estimates in our financial statements.
changes.reasoning: The Year-2 disclosure repeats the same economic risk verbatim and expands it with examples of affected estimates, potential accounting-standard changes, and resulting losses. The risk was therefore retained, not merely inferred from a broader section.
changes.title: Financial Statement Assumptions and Estimates

changes.year1_quote: If actual results differ from the assumptions or estimates underlying our financial statements or if financial accounting and reporting standards are changed, we may experience unexpected material losses.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: If actual results differ from the assumptions or estimates underlying our financial statements or if financial accounting and reporting standards are changed, we may experience unexpected material losses.
changes.reasoning: The Year-2 disclosure preserves the same economic risks: reliance on accounting assumptions and estimates, changes in accounting standards, and potential unexpected material losses. The changes are limited to heading, introductory wording, and cross-reference formatting.
changes.title: Accounting Estimates and Standards Changes

changes.year1_quote: The soundness of other financial institutions and other third parties could adversely affect us.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: The soundness of other financial institutions and other third parties could adversely affect us.
changes.reasoning: The Year-2 disclosure repeats the Year-1 economic risk verbatim and further elaborates it by describing interconnectedness, transaction dependencies, and counterparty exposure. The underlying risk is therefore retained, not merely softened or removed.
changes.title: Soundness of Financial Institutions

changes.year1_quote: Our ability to engage in routine funding and other transactions could be adversely affected by the stability and actions of other financial services institutions. Financial services institutions are interrelated as a result of trading, clearing, servicing, counterparty and other relationships. We have exposure to financial institutions, intermediaries and counterparties that are exposed to risks over which we have little or no control.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: Our ability to engage in routine funding and other transactions could be adversely affected by the stability and actions of other financial services institutions. Financial services institutions are interrelated as a result of trading, clearing, servicing, counterparty and other relationships. We have exposure to financial institutions, intermediaries and counterparties that are exposed to risks over which we have little or no control.
changes.reasoning: The core economic risk—interconnected financial institutions and counterparties whose instability or actions may impair funding and other transactions—is reproduced verbatim in Year-2. The added sentence about third-party soundness broadens the disclosure but does not weaken or alter the retained Year-1 risk.
changes.title: Financial Institution Interconnections and Exposure

changes.year1_quote: In addition, we routinely execute transactions with counterparties in the financial services industry, including brokers and dealers, commercial banks, investment banks, mutual and hedge funds and other institutional clients, resulting in a significant credit concentration with respect to the financial services industry overall.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: In addition, we routinely execute transactions with counterparties in the financial services industry, including brokers and dealers, commercial banks, investment banks, mutual and hedge funds and other institutional clients, resulting in a significant credit concentration with respect to the financial services industry overall.
changes.reasoning: The Year-2 disclosure is substantively identical to Year-1, retaining both the financial-services counterparty credit concentration and the associated default and market-wide liquidity risk.
changes.title: Financial Services Credit Concentration

changes.year1_quote: Likewise, adverse developments affecting the overall strength and soundness of our competitors, the financial services industry as a whole and the general economic climate or sovereign debt could have a negative impact on perceptions about the strength and soundness of our business even if we are not subject to the same adverse developments.
changes.year2_quote_or_null: Likewise, adverse developments affecting the overall strength and soundness of our competitors, the financial services industry as a whole and the general economic climate and the U.S. Treasury market could have a negative impact on perceptions about the strength and soundness of our business even if we are not subject to the same adverse developments.
changes.reasoning: The underlying risk is retained: adverse developments in competitors, the financial system, and broader economic or sovereign/market conditions may damage perceptions of the company despite no direct exposure. The reference changed from “sovereign debt” to “the U.S. Treasury market,” which is a more specific formulation but does not materially alter the disclosed perception and contagion risk.
changes.title: Industry and Economic Perception Risks

changes.year1_quote: For a discussion of the quantitative and qualitative disclosures about market risk, see “MD&A—Market Risk Profile.”
changes.year2_quote_or_null: For a discussion of the quantitative and qualitative disclosures about market risk, see “Part II—Item 7. MD&A—Market Risk Profile.”
changes.reasoning: The disclosure continues to cross-reference the same quantitative and qualitative market-risk discussion. The added “Part II—Item 7” location detail is a formatting or citation change, not a change to the underlying economic risk.
changes.title: Market Risk Disclosure Cross-Reference
